back: A cross that follows the inheritance of one gene (one characteristic).
Homozygous for a gene, so it passes the same allele to all its offspring.
F1: offspring of the parents (P generation). F2: offspring of crossing F1 individuals together.
Key; parents' phenotypes and genotypes; gametes (one allele each); Punnett square; offspring genotypes and phenotypes; ratio.
Heterozygous × heterozygous (for example Tt × Tt): 3 dominant : 1 recessive.
Heterozygous × homozygous recessive (for example Tt × tt).
All offspring heterozygous, all showing the dominant feature.
notes: Example: TT × tt gives all Tt (tall).

front: Why are genetic ratios only probabilities?
back: Fertilisation is random and each event is independent, so real results come close to the expected ratio only when there are large numbers of offspring.

front: In a pedigree, how do you prove an allele is recessive?
back: Find two parents without the feature who have a child with it: both parents must be heterozygous carriers.
notes: Squares = males, circles = females, shaded = shows the feature.

back: Crossing a dominant-phenotype organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive one. Any recessive offspring show it is heterozygous.
notes: All dominant offspring (in large numbers): probably homozygous dominant.
